displayDescription: A copper core and four satin nodes assemble on a slate plinth, with a weighted camera orbit, before the headline settles.
styleRenderer: Three.js 0.186 WebGLRenderer (local node_modules, bundled with local esbuild into scene.bundle.js)

Soft Surface Lighting and Material Detail: MeshPhysicalMaterial copper, satin and rod materials, RoomEnvironment PMREM reflections, PCFSoftShadowMap key light from upper left, NeutralToneMapping, deterministic roughness map, canvas radial contact shadows, fog depth
HTML/CSS DOM typography over a transparent WebGL canvas
motionEngine: GSAP 3 paused timeline (single time source; owns DOM copy opacity and translate)
Extended Position-Based Dynamics (XPBD), custom minimal solver: compliant attachment plus a unilateral rod-length contact and floor contact, baked at load at a fixed 240 Hz and sampled by time
Procedural part assembly in the glTF scene-assembly pattern: fixed key states for core, rods and nodes evaluated at composition time
Authored deterministic camera navigation, standing in for live orbit/raycast controls in a video
limitations: Blender, bpy, Cycles and EEVEE were not used, as the user instructed. Real-time Three.js PBR rasterisation approximates the offline path-traced look: no global illumination, caustics or ray-traced reflections. Reflections come from a procedural RoomEnvironment probe.
No glTF asset files were supplied, so the geometry is procedural Three.js primitives. Part animation follows the glTF assembly pattern but no GLTFLoader is used.

XPBD is a small custom point-mass solver (attachment compliance 0.0055, damping 9/s, reduced gravity), not a maintained library. It is a stylised, physically approximate settle, eased to exact seats from 2.2–2.5s.
Raycast Object Interaction is represented only by its video-delivery equivalent, an authored deterministic camera path. No pointer raycasting happens in the export.
Video-Textured Screens and CRT Overlays were not used: the subject has no screen and no footage was supplied, and adding a CRT surface would not serve the scene.
Contact shadows are canvas radial-gradient decals combined with soft shadow maps. They approximate ambient occlusion.
The Three.js bundle contains Math.random, used only for internal object UUIDs. It does not affect any rendered pixel.
Stage colour and lighting were chosen from the background review's role lessons. Tone mapping slightly alters the rendered material colours relative to the palette hex values.
No rendering or browser test was run by the agent; the host QA is authoritative.
